chapter: Baton Rouge, first New York trip, the road years
title: The Blue Moon in Baton Rouge and an early Ray Charles jukebox record
summary: He played a Black club with Joe Houston; Audre recalls hearing early Ray Charles on a jukebox.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: It says here also that you played at a black club called the Blue Moon in Baton Rouge with a guy named Joe Houston, who had a trumpeter named Walter Miller, who you think played with Ray Charles later. So again, you were moving back and forth between these worlds.
Wasn’t that when you first heard Ray Charles also? What was the name of that song...
A girl with the red dress on... What’s the name of that? That was a real early one, and it was on a jukebox down there.
Yeah. Well, I don’t remember that. But it was called “Baby, Let Me Hold Your Hand,” I think.
No. The one that you dragged me someplace to hear it on a jukebox, and it was “I see the girl with the red dress on, she can show that thing...”
Oh, yeah. That was later. That was later!
